newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors summon sacked defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors summon sacked defence minister.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Thursday summoned sacked defence minister Lee Yang-ho to question him over an arms scandal, witnesses said.
"Lee arrived at the prosecutors' office for questioning this evening," a witness said.
"He did not respond to reporters' questions and was taken to a prosecutor's office," he said.
President Kim Young-sam dismissed Lee on Thursday last week, hours before the main opposition party National Congress for New Politics accused him of taking bribes. Kim has ordered an inquiry.

The National Congress accused Lee and a Korean-American arms dealer of splitting a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd lao arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Daewoo admitted giving money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe. Lee has denied accusations of wrongdoing.
A prosecution official said three Daewoo officials were being questioned on Thursday in connection with the kickback probe.

They were Sok Chin-chol, last year's president of Daewoo Heavy, Daewoo Group chairman Yoon Young-suk and Chung Ho-shin, vice-president of Daewoo Heavy, a group unit and a leading government arms contractor.
"Whether the prosecution will take further legal steps against Mr Lee willter face-to-face cross questioning between him and the Daewoo officials," the prosecution official said.
Yoon, who is also chief executive officer of Daewoo Heavy, told reporters his company was deceived by the arms dealer but gave no further details.
The affair has eesident Kim, who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption crusade that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being found guilty in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both are appealing their convictions.
Daewoo Group r Kim Woo-choong is currently appealing a two-year jail sentence imposed for bribing Roh. He was one of nine businessmen convicted on similar charges.
